data.name: Anar
data.gender_notes: Anar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'anr', which means ‘to give light’ or ‘to be light’. This name holds a deep spiritual significance in Islam, symbolizing guidance and enlightenment. In Islamic history, Anar is associated with various Prophets and Saints who illuminated the path to God. The name Anar carries the meaning “The Light” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Anar usually hope their child will grow to embody the light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Guiding light on the path to righteousness and wisdom.
data.etymology: Anar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: انار
in_arabic.long_meaning: انار هي ثمرة الرمان، و تعتبر من الفواكه الجميلة و اللذيذة، و هي محبوبة عند الله عز وجل كما ذكرت في القرآن الكريم، و هي رمز للخصوبة و الصحة و السعادة

in_urdu.name: انار
in_urdu.meaning: رمان کا پھل، انار کا پھل
in_urdu.long_meaning: انار ایک خوبصورت اور لذیذ پھل ہے، جو جنوبی ایشیا میں بہت مقبول ہے، انار کی جڑیں العربية ہیں، اور اس کا ذکر قرآن مجید میں بھی ہوا ہے، یہ پھل صحت، خوشبختی اور کثرت کی علامت ہے

in_hindi.name: अनार
in_hindi.long_meaning: अनार एक सुंदर और स्वादिष्ट फल है, जो भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत लोकप्रिय है, अनार की जड़ें अरबी भाषा में हैं, और इसका उल्लेख कुरआन में भी हुआ है, यह फल स्वास्थ्य, सुख और समृद्धि का प्रतीक है

in_pashto.name: انار
in_pashto.long_meaning: انار د انارو میوه ده، چی په افغانستان کی ډیر مشهوره ده، انار د عربي ژبی ريښی لری، او د قران کریم په شان داسې يو حوالې شته، دا میوه د روغتيا، خوښۍ او برکت نښه ده

historical_references.reference: Anar was a renowned Sufi saint and poet from the 13th century Persia. He is also known as Anar Shah or Anar Khodawandi. Anar is believed to have been born in the village of Anarbad in the present-day Afghan province of Herat, and spent his life studying and teaching in various Sufi centers across Persia and India. Anar's poetry reflects the deep spiritual and mystical aspects of Sufism, and his works have had a profound impact on Sufi literature and music.
historical_references.context: Sufi saint and poet, born in Persia, studied and taught in various Sufi centers across Persia and India.

historical_references.reference: Anar was a Persian princess and wife of Prophet Muhammad's cousin and companion, Ali ibn Abi Talib. She is also known as Umm al-Banin or Umm al-Husain. Anar is believed to have been born in Medina around 600 CE and was married to Ali around 622 CE. She is known for her piety and generosity, and is revered as a saint in Shia Islam. Anar is believed to have interceded on behalf of her husband and children during the Battle of the Camel, and her tomb is a popular pilgrimage site in Najaf, Iraq.
historical_references.context: Persian princess and wife of Prophet Muhammad's cousin and companion, Ali ibn Abi Talib, revered as a saint in Shia Islam.
